turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi there! How's it going today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you help me figure out a gluten free dinner spot? My roommate just got diagnosed with celiac.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure. The key is finding places that understand cross contamination, not just ones with a gluten free label on a few dishes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How would I even know that?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Call and ask whether they use a separate fryer and prep area. A confident, detailed answer is a really good sign.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wait, wait, what kinds of food are usually safe?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Thai, Mexican and Indian often have lots of naturally gluten free dishes, think rice, corn tortillas and lentils. Still ask about sauces though, soy sauce has wheat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh no, she loves soy sauce.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: There's tamari, which is a wheat free version. Lots of Japanese places keep it if you ask.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: she thought sushi was off the table forever.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all. Just mention celiac when booking, so the kitchen can be careful.
